ballot_results.name: Langley (City)
ballot_results.question:
BACKGROUND INFORMATION
As our population continues to grow, Langley City is considering investing in two large community facilities. This initiative is called Invest Langley City. The City would use future borrowing and other potential funding sources such as government grants, donations, fees charged to developers, internal reserves, casino revenues, and user fees to fund the new facilities.
Langley City invites voters to respond to this non-binding community opinion vote about these potential community investment facilities.
The results will be used to help the incoming Council understand community views before making decisions about whether to continue planning the facility expansions. After the non-binding vote, if a future Council directs staff to continue planning and later decides to move forward with one or both projects and borrowing is required, a separate binding approval process would be required before the project(s) could proceed.

ballot_results.name: Langley (City)
ballot_results.question:
INVESTMENT DESCRIPTIONS AND TAX IMPLICATIONS
Investment Option 1:
The Al Anderson Memorial Pool Expansion includes a new building with a steam room and sauna, hot tub, leisure pool, and change rooms. It also includes improvements to the existing building and pool so it can operate year-round.
The current estimated capital cost is $73 million. If the City cannot secure other funding sources, the tax impact for homeowners would be about 2.95% per year for four years then remain the same until the loan is paid (over a period of thirty (30) years or less).
•	For an average single-family home: this amounts to an increase of about $100 per year for the initial four years
•	For an average multi-family home (including owned condos): this amounts to an increase of about $45 per year for the initial four years
•	Commercial property owners would also pay. Renters will not pay these taxes, although tax impacts may affect rental rates charged by landlords


1.	Do you support Langley City in moving forward with the Al Anderson Memorial Pool Expansion, resulting in the potential tax implications as described in Option 1 above?

ballot_results.name: Langley (City)
ballot_results.summary: Timms Community Centre Expansion and new performing arts centre
ballot_results.question:
Investment Option 2:
The Timms Community Centre Expansion combined with a new Performing Arts and Cultural Centre includes improving and expanding the existing fitness and recreation area and a new half-gym. It also includes a 500-seat performance theatre with concession, multipurpose rooms, a gallery and exhibit space, commercial spaces, an outdoor plaza, and underground parking.
The current estimated capital cost is $107 million. If the City cannot secure other funding sources, the tax impact for homeowners would be about 4.29% per year for four years and then remain the same until the loan is paid (over a period of thirty (30) years or less).
•	For an average single-family home: this amounts to an increase of about $150 per year for the initial four years
•	For an average multi-family home (including owned condos): this amounts to an increase of about $65 per year for the initial four years
•	Commercial property owners would also pay. Renters will not pay these taxes, although tax impacts may affect rental rates charged by landlords


2.	Do you support Langley City in moving forward with the Timms Community Centre Expansion combined with a new Performing Arts and Cultural Centre, resulting in the potential tax implications as described in Option 2 above?

ballot_results.name: Langley (City)
ballot_results.summary: Tax increase to fund pool and community centre expansion
ballot_results.question:
Investment Option 3:
If the City proceeds with both investments and cannot secure other funding sources, the combined tax impact would be about 7.24% per year for four years, then remain the same until the loan is paid.
•	For an average single-family home: this amounts to an increase of about $250 per year for the initial four years
•	For an average multi-family home (including owned condos): this amounts to an increase of about $110 per year for the initial four years
•	Commercial property owners would also pay. Renters will not pay these taxes, although tax impacts may affect rental rates charged by landlords

3.	Do you support Langley City in moving forward with both the Al Anderson Memorial Pool Expansion AND the Timms Community Centre Expansion combined with a new Performing Arts and Cultural Centre, resulting in the tax implications as described in Option 3 above?

ballot_results.name: Vancouver
ballot_results.question:
Vancouver has experienced unprecedented levels of street disorder, open-air hard drug use, and disruption to community safety and individual health. Therefore:

1. Are you in favour of the City of Vancouver strengthening its laws to forbid open-air hard drug (Heroin, Meth, Fentanyl, and Crack) use in public spaces?

2. Should the City of Vancouver formally ask the Province of B.C. to convert portions of the old St. Paul’s Hospital  or another similar site into a secure medical facility that provides acute voluntary and 100-plus involuntary care beds for individuals posing a serious risk to themselves or others due to severe substance us and mental health disorders?

ballot_results.name: Vancouver
ballot_results.question:
The $790 million amount has been organized into three questions, as follows: 

1. TRANSPORTATION AND STREET INFRASTRUCTURE 
Are you in favour of Council having the authority, without further assent of the electors, to pass by-laws between January 1, 2027, and December 31, 2030, to borrow an aggregate $292,000,000 for the following purposes? 

A. Bridge and structure infrastructure 

To provide for major maintenance, rehabilitation, reconstruction and enhancement of the City’s bridge and structure infrastructure, including repairs and structural work on the Granville Bridge and Cambie Bridge. 

 $154,000,000 

B. Pavement and sidewalk infrastructure 

To provide for major maintenance, reconstruction and enhancement of the arterial and neighbourhood transportation networks, and sidewalks. 

 $92,000,000

C. Traffic signals and street lighting 

To provide for major maintenance, replacement and enhancement of traffic signals and nstreet lighting that are beyond economical repair or no longer meet operational requirements. 

$46,000,000 

Total: $292,000,000 

If this question receives the assent of the electors, Council has the power, without further assent of the electors, to pass by-laws, as and when Council considers appropriate, to borrow money for the projects described up to $292,000,000. 

EXPLANATORY NOTE FOR QUESTIONS 2 AND 3: 

• Community facilities include buildings such as community centres, pools, rinks, libraries, childcare facilities, cultural facilities, and social facilities. 

• Civic facilities include buildings such as fire halls, police buildings, administrative facilities and service yards. 

2. COMMUNITY SERVING AND CIVIC ESSENTIAL INFRASTRUCTURE 
Are you in favour of Council having the authority, without further assent of the electors, to pass by-laws between January 1, 2027, and December 31, 2030, to borrow an aggregate $438,000,000 for the following purposes? 

A. Renewal and upgrades of community facilities 

To provide for replacement, renewal or rehabilitation of community facilities, including aging community centres, pools or other community facility projects including buildings such as rinks, libraries, childcare facilities, and social facilities. 

 $338,000,000 

B. Renewal and upgrades of other community serving and civic facilities 

To provide for replacement, renewal or rehabilitation of other civic essential facilities, including fire halls, service yards, and other cultural facilities including Vancouver Civic Theatres. 
 
 $100,000,000 

Total: $438,000,000 

If this question receives the assent of the electors, Council has the power, without further assent of the electors, to pass by-laws, as and when Council considers appropriate, to borrow money for the projects described up to $438,000,000. 

3. PARKS AND OPEN PUBLIC SPACES INFRASTRUCTURE 
Are you in favour of Council having the authority, without further assent of the electors, to pass by-laws between January 1, 2027, and December 31, 2030, to borrow an aggregate $60,000,000 for the following purposes? 

 A. Renewal, maintenance and upgrades of parks 

To provide for renewal, ongoing capital maintenance, renovations or other upgrades of parks, park buildings and features within parks such as the seawall, pathways, playgrounds, playfields and sport courts. 

$60,000,000

Total: $60,000,000 

If this question receives the assent of the electors, Council has the power, without further assent of the electors, to pass by-laws, as and when Council considers appropriate, to borrow money for the projects described up to $60,000,000.

ballot_results.name: Metro Vancouver (Regional District)
ballot_results.summary: MVRD bylaw 1433: Waste collection tax for water-access properties
ballot_results.question:
(For the electors of water-access properties in Bowyer Island, Passage Island, Indian Arm, and Pitt Lake): 

Are you in favour of the Metro Vancouver Regional District adopting MVRD Bylaw No. 1433, 2026 to establish within portions of Electoral Area A, a service for the purpose of the coordination, transportation, and disposal of waste items generated from water-access properties within the area, and to authorize a maximum annual taxation of $20,000 or $0.6/$1,000 of net taxable value of improvements, whichever is greater?
